children.text: Rising prices is plaguing the United States like the Black Death in 14th century Europe. The pain is felt everywhere, and the rise of minimum wage hasn't matched the cost of living in years. Generations prior to gen-z are aware of how cheap basic necessities used to cost, and data points to the middle class is slowly getting priced out of everything. Competition amongst the middle class is getting fiercer with the threat of being pushed into poverty looming over Americans daily actions.

Compounding this is the increase in car dependent cities, and I’d assert people all across the country are looking for forms of community and belonging. The stress of our economic conditions are leading people to look for cheap forms of entertainment. And what is more free than social media? Tiktok has about 1.9 billion active users and with the number of monthly active users on Instagram being over 2 billion. The rise of AI, cost of living, and the attention economy are funneling Americans into social media accounts and in response emerges a new form of art:

Editing has surged in popularity in recent years, and this project explores the beautiful history connecting editing with fandom culture. Despite it's roots within fandom, Capitalism is relentless in the pursuit of monetizing all forms of art. This project explores the current-day relationship between fan editing as an art form and companies turning this art form into: an ad. Hidden in the infinite scroll mechanism is ads within these forms of entertainment.

title: An Ad for An Ad- The Sad Implications of Fan Edits as An Art Form
